transfers.source_mechanism: adaptive network formation through iterative feedback and resource allocation
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: distributed network adaptation through local probing and reinforcement based on flow measurements
transfers.required_translation: replace biological nutrient transport with traffic flow optimization, replace network nodes with signalized intersections, replace resource allocation with signal timing adjustment, replace probing with traffic flow measurement cycles
transfers.expected_effect: traffic signal network that adapts to real-time conditions through local decision-making, optimizing traffic flow without central coordination
boundary_conditions: limited communication between adjacent intersections only
failure_conditions: resource depletion (computational limitations at intersection controllers)
environmental disruption (unpredictable traffic patterns exceeding adaptation capacity)
transfers.testable_prediction: In a simulation with random incidents, the adaptive signal timing system will reduce average intersection delay by at least 15% compared to the fixed 6-month optimized plan within 30 minutes of an incident, while maintaining stability without oscillations over a 24-hour period with varying traffic patterns.
